text: Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky introduced Prospect Theory in their 1979 Econometrica paper, replacing expected utility theory as the descriptive model of choice under risk for the seminar syllabus.

text: Adopted Daniel Kahneman's Thinking, Fast and Slow as the opening textbook for the undergraduate behavioral economics course; the System 1 and System 2 framing anchors the first four weeks of lectures.

queries.text: which popular textbook opens the undergraduate course and which dual-process framing does it lean on
kahneman thinking fast slow system 1 system 2 textbook course

text: The loss aversion asymmetry is the core of Prospect Theory: losses loom roughly twice as large as equivalent gains, with the coefficient lambda estimated between 2.0 and 2.5 in the classic experiments.

loss aversion lambda prospect theory asymmetry gain experiment coefficient

text: Chose to open the endowment effect lecture with Richard Thaler's Cornell mug experiment rather than the Knetsch pen study, since the roughly two-to-one seller-buyer price gap lands more cleanly with undergraduates.

endowment effect thaler cornell mug experiment seller buyer lecture

text: The framing effects literature shows that describing an outcome as ninety percent survival versus ten percent mortality flips choices even when logically equivalent; Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman used the Asian Disease study to nail this down.

framing effect asian disease survival mortality equivalent choice tversky

text: Picked the Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman wheel-of-fortune experiment as the anchoring demo for the online homework over the real-estate anchoring study; the randomised-spin setup runs cleanly in a browser without requiring property photos.

queries.text: which anchoring demo won the online homework slot over the real-estate anchoring variant
anchoring tversky wheel fortune online homework real estate pick

text: Decided to split the availability heuristic from representativeness into separate lectures rather than the bundled treatment in earlier syllabi; the 1973 Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman recall-based variant deserves its own session given how often media-vividness examples derail discussion.

queries.text: which heuristic was split out of a bundled lecture to get its own session in the course
availability heuristic tversky kahneman 1973 split lecture media vivid

text: Prefer the Linda conjunction fallacy from Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman over the lawyer-engineer base-rate problem when introducing representativeness; Linda produces cleaner error rates in an intro audience even though both illustrate the same 1972 heuristic.

representativeness linda conjunction bank teller feminist prefer lawyer

text: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein published Nudge in 2008, formalising libertarian paternalism as a design philosophy in which choice architecture steers decisions without restricting options.

queries.text: which 2008 book paired Thaler with Sunstein to formalise libertarian paternalism through choice architecture
nudge thaler sunstein 2008 libertarian paternalism choice architecture

Save More Tomorrow, designed by Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi, commits employees to raise 401(k) contributions with future pay rises, exploiting default effects and hyperbolic discounting together.

text: Settled on George Ainslie's 1970s hyperbolic discounting account as the baseline intertemporal model for the course, since its preference reversals predictions match the pigeon and human choice data far better than the textbook exponential.

hyperbolic discounting ainslie preference reversal baseline course exponential

text: David Laibson's beta-delta model formalises quasi-hyperbolic discounting with a present-bias parameter beta alongside an exponential delta, giving a tractable alternative to the full hyperbolic discounting curves from the Ainslie tradition.

queries.text: which two-parameter discounting model did Laibson propose as a tractable stand-in for pure hyperbolic curves
laibson beta delta quasi hyperbolic discount present bias tractable

text: Hal Arkes and Catherine Blumer's 1985 Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes paper is the standing reference for the sunk-cost fallacy on the course's secondary reading list.

text: The mental accounting framework, developed by Richard Thaler, treats money as non-fungible across psychological buckets; the framework predicts why households hold high-interest credit debt while keeping low-yield savings.

mental accounting thaler non fungible bucket credit debt saving

status quo bias samuelson zeckhauser 1988 pipeline opt in module

text: Prefer Eric Johnson and Daniel Goldstein's 2003 organ-donation study as the canonical default effects illustration over the 401(k) enrollment papers; the cross-country gap between presumed-consent and opt-in countries is harder to attribute to confounds.

default effect johnson goldstein 2003 organ donation prefer 401k

text: The choice overload effect was documented in Sheena Iyengar and Mark Lepper's 2000 jam study, where a 24-variety display drew more browsers but a 6-variety display produced roughly ten times the purchase rate.

choice overload iyengar lepper 2000 jam study 24 variety purchase

art of choosing iyengar supplementary reading arranged marriage autonomy

text: The Behavioural Insights Team, known as BIT and nicknamed the Nudge Unit, was founded in 2010 within the UK Cabinet Office with Richard Thaler as academic advisor and later spun out as a social-purpose company.

east framework bit easy attractive social timely policy nudge civil
